claim_tested: The proposed calibration metric's verdict tracks calibration quality, not ground-truth overlap, under a genuinely clustered population (multi-row customer clusters with correlated within-cluster noise) -- independent evidence, materially different from the implementer's own one-row-per-cluster construction.
gap_in_implementer_evidence_this_fills: The implementer's own case_c/case_d (diagnose_task087_check5_7_calibration_adversarial.py) assign a UNIQUE customer_id per record, so every cluster_cells entry has exactly one record -- the cluster bootstrap's clustering never actually engages. The real dataset has genuine repeat-customer clustering (3200 customers over 10000 rows, most customers contributing 3-4 rows). This script re-derives Check 7's conclusion under real cluster structure instead.
conclusion: Both cases resolve as required (C well-calibrated despite zero overlap, D poorly calibrated despite 90% overlap) under genuine multi-row clustering. This independently confirms, with a materially different construction, that the design's verdict tracks calibration quality, not ground-truth overlap.
